properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2018-12-17 to Eqt Production Co in Center Twp, Greene county. 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Eqt Production Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2018-12-17
Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 837120
Permit API: 059-27170
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2018-12-17
Comments: On 12/16/18 at approximately 0715 a water truck at the site rolled off the access road, causing an impaired water release. According to Oil & Gas Inspector Supervisor Scott Sabocheck's Emergency Response Team report, approximately 110 barrels of produced fluid and approximately 100-130 gallons of diesel fuel were released to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. EQT reported the release to the Department at 0745. On 12/17/18 at approximately 1050 hours I conducted an incident response inspection. I met with David Guidas of EQT who explained that a water truck was on its way to the AST with a load of impaired water when it got too close to the edge of the access road and rolled over the edge onto water lines servicing the AST and frack. The spill occurred in a sediment trap, limiting the extent of the spill. Due to the presence of rain water in the sediment trap the spill impacted Waters of the Commonwealth. Approximately 90 barrels of rain water, impaired water, and diesel fuel were recovered by a vac truck. SPSI had conducted remediation of the spill at the time of investigation. Guidas indicated additional screenings were to be conducted and further excavation, as water with elevated conductivity was still being observed. Guidas indicated once the final remediation was complete Corey Giles of EQT would be handling the Act 2 process. OGIS Sabocheck indicated in his ERT report that EQT agreed to pressure test the lines prior to placing the damaged lines back in use. At the time of inspection David Guidas of EQT indicated a section of line had been replaced.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Pressure Build-Up Tests (PBUTs) being performed on both wells on the DeWolf pad, the Evelyn Wyo. 4H and the Evelyn Wyo. 2H. These PBUTs are being performed to access recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool) deployment that was performed on both wells on 12/18/20. (Depths of CET deployments were attached to individual well inspections of 2/4/2021. Insp. ID's 2H - 3143784, 4H - 3143787). Both of the Evelyn wells Surface x Intermediate, (13 3/8 x 9 5/8), the Intermediate x Production, (9 5/8 x 5 1/2) annuli and the (20x13) annulus of the Evelyn 2H were shut in on 5/24/21 @ ~ 09:00.All shut-in pressures were monitored and recorded throughout testing period by CALLCs SCADA system. The Evelyn Wyo. 4H wells Conductor x Surface (20 x 13 3/8) annulus has an open casing top in cellar, the Evelyn Wyo. 2H Conductor by Surface (20 x13 3/8) annulus is capped and set up for venting to atmosphere via a 1" pipe to surface and a Sentry valve. Both wells remained in production through the PBUT period. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Matt Clark and Victor Kanvik and Creston Consultant Reps. Shane Reimold and Alex Pashchuk. Starting at approx. 09:00 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. 5/27/21)). Gas detections were then confirmed by The Department, using a MSA ALTAIR 5X gas meter, last calibrated on 5/14/21. Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for both of the Evelyn Wyo. wells on this pad: - Evelyn Wyo 4H: - (20x13): open casing top in cellar, no bubbling noted. * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 3.0 psi.; 83% gas; Sample taken @ 09:42. - (9x5): 96 psi.; 86% gas; Sample taken @ 09:50. ** The (9x5) annulus vent was opened on 5/26/21 @ 19:35, and shut in today @ 08:56. Sample was taken for this annulus @ 09:34. - Evelyn Wyo. 2H: - (20x13): 35 psi.; 61% gas; Sample taken @ 09:18. * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 138 psi.; 75% gas; Sample taken @ 09:26. - (9x5); 316 psi.; 73% gas; Sample taken @ 09:34. - All annuli were returned to venting by 09:50.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 914302
Permit API: 081-21812
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/19/2021
Comments: On April 19, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an investigation of a reported spill (CTS No. 356072) at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported on April 19, 2021, after removing the second AST off the well pad an area of high conductivity and staining was observed in the highly compacted soil where the tank was located. The estimated volume of the spill was about 500 gallons of production fluid. The area of impact was about 120 ft. X 150 ft. circle with varying levels of conductivity. A contractor was onsite beginning to excavate the impacted soils. The contractor was removing about 6 to 8 inches of impacted soil. The area of impact was screened by Beech Resources for conductivity. Areas where the compacted soil had already been removed had a conductivity near 320 uS/cm to 910 uS/cm. Conductivity of areas that had not yet been excavated at the time were around 1.69 mS/cm. There were no seeps off the well pad observed. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect confirmatory samples on April 20, 2021. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection Reports 3139277 and 3141035 still remain.

Comments: On 5/18/2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill at the Mazure William well pad in Hanover Township, Washington County. The spill was reportedly discovered on 5/17/2026, at 6:20 AM; and reported to the Department on 5/17/2026, at 8:05 AM. The spill was reportedly caused by a pipe fitting failure on the flash separator unit. An estimated 15 gallons of a produced water/condensate mixture released to the surface of the well pad. Accompanying the Department during this inspection is Range Resources representative Nick Reda. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP-2) for this site was terminated on 9/02/2020.The following was observed during the inspection:The flash separator unit has been disconnected and moved to accommodate remediation operations (photos 4 and 5). properties.content:

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-04-04
Comments: On 04/04/19 at approximately 1200 hours I conducted a routine complete inspection of the site. The Act 9 sign was in place. The site was gated and locked. The stream crossing over Lutz Run had been destroyed and was missing. Contrary to 105.172(a), Diversified failed to immediately notify the Department of the collapse of the crossing. Remaining culvert pipes were not properly maintained and sediment and debris were obstructing the flow of water through the structures. Materials used to construct the crossing had been washed downstream. Large stones from the crossing were present in the stream. The brine tanks were heavily corroded and had poor structural integrity. Multiple holes were observed in both brine tanks. Diversified failed to notify the Department of tank deficiencies within 3 days of discovery and failed to address and remedy the deficiencies contrary to 78A57(i). The Department requests 1 year (12 months) of brine tank inspections per 78A57(i) be provided to the Department. To achieve compliance the brine tanks must be replaced or remedied in accordance with manufacturer's specifications and applicable engineering design criteria. If the tanks are replaced adherence to chapter 78A regulations regarding secondary containment will be necessary. The Department requests 1 year (12 months) of periodic inspections of the crossing per 105.53 be provided to the Department. The Department requests Diversified provide the date the stream crossing was observed to be missing.

Comments: On April 25, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth were observed during the time of IR 3965337.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who stated that forecasted storms have delayed start of remediation to Monday, 4/28/2025. In response, the impacted area was covered, and oil absorbent booms and E and S controls were installed downslope.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). A gas odor was detected onsite during this inspection. The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5 and 6). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank has been covered with plastic sheeting in preparation for the forecasted rains. Additional oil absorbent booms have also been placed down slope of the covered impacted area (see photos 8-15). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected down slope of impacted area (see photos 16 and 17).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the impacted area has been adequately,protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: An oil release to ground from a malfunctioning valve on the discharge pipe of one of the two tanks located in secondary containment at this well site was reported by Kenneth Fleeman on April 11, 2019. Oil was released from the tank by a malfunctioning valve which resulted in oil flow to the southwest end of the secondary containment where it disappeared into the stony soil. There is dead vegetation and oily pools of water observed to the east, south and west of the secondary containment. A 200 foot path of dead vegetation extends south of the well site. The path of dead vegetation disappears on the slope south of the well site and does not appear to have reached any waterways. A patch of dead vegetation and several oily pools of water is evident 15' east of the secondary containment. There is a 50' to 70' path of vegetation to the southwest however the oil does not appear to have moved any farther. Abarta Production Supervisor, Scott Patterson, stated that all tanks and piping were intact at the time of his inspection of the well on April 1, 2019 and the tank had approximately 13" of oil (10.75 barrels) at that time. All oil above the the discharge pipe was released to ground. Based on conductivity testing this was an oil release only, no brine was released. This is a violation of PA Oil and Gas Regulations and a clean-up process will be required. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TITUS ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/25/2025
Violation Code: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 8241979
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #3978563 conducted on May 15 2025 at 0848. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, or failure. While onsite the well appeared to be producing off of the 4" production string. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 94% combustible gas. To evaluate the potential for subsurface gas migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the well-bore in the cardinal directions. Each hole was placed to a depth of approximately 3 feet. Soil gas measurements were obtained using a Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on July 24, 2025. The results were as follows: South and East slam bar holes: Non-detect for combustible gas. North slam bar hole: Peak reading of 3% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. West slam bar hole: Peaking reading of 18% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. Due to the lack of adequate sustained concentration, a viable sample for isotopic analysis could not be collected. On May 22, 2025 the Department received an email from the operator stating that "Titus would prefer to have the Johnson #1 well plugged". As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with it. The Department requests a detailed timeline specifying when the well will be properly plugged or when corrective measures will be undertaken to bring the well into full regulatory compliance.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection at the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located Ulysses Twp, Potter Co. on 8/1/2019 @1050 hours. The weather was 72 degrees and sunny. Present onsite for the inspection were myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Terra Tokarz, Whipper Hill Consultant, Scott West, JKLM. JKLM called the Department's spill line, at 0515 hours the same day, to report a release of approximately 42 gallons of stimulation fluid. The report stated, during ongoing completion activities a water line separated from the well head spraying the fluid mostly onto containment, with a portion depositing on the pad surface. As of today's inspection, Whipper Hill Consulting was present onsite screening the SW corner of the well pad just off containment. Ms. Tokarz stated a vac truck had removed all fluid on the pad surface from the release. Ms. Tokarz was completing a grid survey of soil conductivity readings on the impacted pad surface in preparation for removing the impacted pad material into onsite waste containers. Elevated conductivity fluid was observed inside the pad containment and was being removed with a vac truck. JKLM stated the surrounding E&S controls were screened and found not to be impacted. JKLM estimated the volume of fluid released to the pad surface was >5 gallons but less that 1 barrel. The DEP received confirmation from JKLM the impacted material has been removed and soil conductivity readings, in the impacted area, are <1.5mS/cm. The spill has been remediated. Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 3HU, API#105-21924: 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a) SWMA 301 CSL 402(b) We departed the site at 1230 hours.

Comments: The operator reported to DEP on 7/10/19 that a 1-2 barrel spill of production fluid occurred at the E09 S well pad. This inspection occurred the morning of 7/11. It appears as though a fitting on a dump line from a bulk unit failed, which allowed produced water to spill into the containment within the unit. Once the containment of approximately 600 gallons was filled, water began to spill out on either side of the unit. Workers on site noticed the spill and immediately shut the site down so that containment and remediation could begin. It is estimated that 1-2 barrels of production fluid was spilled to the ground. Equipment was brought to the site and three roll-off containers were filled with contaminated soil. The operator used a soil probe to determine where conductivity was elevated and dug an area approximately 30x60 feet at the time of this inspection. They did not dig under the bulk unit, as they were going to attempt to flush any production fluid out from under it rather than move the unit at this time. Work will continue on this site until soil tests come back clean. No threats to nearby water sources were noted, as this spill was contained within a small area on the pad.

Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Elkland Township

Inspection Date: 5/20/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of at least 5 gallons of produced fluid. Upon arrival I met with Creston Environmental representatives and with Mike Deming of Chesapeake (Expand).While removing secondary containment puddled fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered adjacent to the northern side of the 5HC well cellar. This location is shown on the right side of the well in Photo 1 and in Photo 3. Upon further investigation a hole was discovered in the containment in that area. After discovering the fluid a vac truck was used to remove the fluid and two sumps were started on the northern and southern sides of the wellhead. The sumps encountered additional fluid at around 2.5 feet deep. Fluid has continued to be removed from the sumps. Creston provided conductivity readings for the removed fluid. The initial puddle was 1,280 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The fluid collecting in the sumps was around 14,780 uS/cm on the northern side and 10,446 uS/cm on the southern side. Soil conductivity for the pad surface beyond the sump its self ranged between 89 and 238 uS/cm. There did not appear to be any impacts on the other exposed portions of the pad or the surrounding area. There were no seeps or standing water observed in the area around the pad including in the PCSM.The sumps will be expanded to facilitate monitoring and removal of additional fluid. There will be screening and fluid removal throughout the flowback period. After flowback equipment is removed further characterization and remediation will be completed under Act 2 per Mike Deming. DEP will conduct followup inspections over the coming days and weeks to additionally asses the stability and state of the impacted and downgrade areas.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). The violations may be closed after completion of Act 2 remediation.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2026
Violation Code: 102.22(a)1 - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to remove temporary E & S BMPs once permanent stabilization had been established.
Violation ID: 8284097
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

Comments: The Department of Environmental (DEP) conducted a Follow-up Inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 6/12/2019 @1000 hours. The weather was rain 62 degrees. Present onsite for the inspection was Ross McMann, DEP Geologic Specialist and myself. Activity onsite consisted of Tilden Marcellus conducting stimulation activities on the 4H well. The DEP was onsite to follow-up on remediation activities associated with the 6/3/2019 release of an estimate 10 barrels of stimulation fluid outside containment. As of today's inspection, a lined ditch was observed installed across the ESE fill slope of the well pad. The ditch was collecting potentially impacted runoff from the well pad. Fluid in the ditch had a field measured conductivity of 460uS/cm. The E&S control at the base of the SE fill slope was observed full of fluid with a field measured conductivity of 420uS/cm. A pump was positioned, on containment, just upslope of the E&S control to remove water as needed. Onsite personnel stated no elevated conductivity fluid has been observed in the E&S control. Fluid along the ESE edge of the well pad had a field measured conductivity of 10.45mS/cm indicating the continued presence of a pollutional substance. Soils just off the edge of the well pad had elevated conductivity of >2.0mS/cm in the upper inch of soil. Onsite personnel stated once stimulation activities were complete, Tilden would initiate removal of the containment/rig mats, screening of the E/SE section of the pad (and surrounding areas), and removal of all impacted material. Onsite personnel were notified of any deficiencies. Violations, cited 6/4/2019 in IR#2889847, remain OUTSTANDING against the 3H well, API#117-20476. No other violations are noted at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation ID: 954502
Permit API: 019-21931
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Slippery Rock Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/09/2022
Comments: At the time of inspection, label affixed to well with Permit No. 37-019-21931 (Photo 1). Operator in process of changing out well labels to reflect Big Dog Energy, LLC ownership. The annulus valves at the wellhead are open and venting to the atmosphere (Photo 2). Operator is currently in the process of installing production equipment onsite. The operator submitted an Application for Inactive Well Status on April 22, 2022 and was received by the Department on April 27, 2022. Upon review of information and inspection of the well, the Department has determined that the well meets the requirements of OGA 3214(a)(1) and 3214(a)(2). The application is being forwarded on for additional comments. Violations issued: Since Operator obtained ownership of well in August 2021 and Application for Inactive Well Status was not received by the Department until April 27, 2022, the well is considered abandoned. This is a violation of the Oil and Gas Act 3220(A). Operator is required to develop and implement Emergency Response Plan and review and submit updates annually to the Department by March 1. This is a violation of PA Chapter 78a55(i)5iii.
